body:
This is very similar to issue #89479. `dFdx` is registered in the `frag_only_func_defs`, which are checked in a few places in the shader_language file in combination with the `is_supported_frag_only_funcs` variable:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e531f3eb7b13a9adaaf5b15ac9b3aebc4c2030cd/servers/rendering/shader_language.cpp#L9129C2-L9130C89

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e531f3eb7b13a9adaaf5b15ac9b3aebc4c2030cd/servers/rendering/shader_language.cpp#L6248C7-L6264C8

`shader_identifier_type` is deliberately not checked/set to anything when processing gdshaderinc files.

Options include:
* Perform a similar `shader_type_identifier != StringName()` check specifically for this built-in validation.
* Include `is_shader_inc` or empty shader_type_identifier in the criteria for `is_supported_frag_only_funcs` (broader impact).
* Ignore it because it doesn't actually break shader compilation (though it is very confusing for a user, and similar to the linked issue will obfuscate "actual" errors lower down in the include).

Can confirm, this issue is happening to me as well:

Calling dFdx and dFdy in a function defined inside a gdshaderinc will yield the error above.

Worked fine in godot 4.3.

> This is very similar to issue [#89479](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/89479). `dFdx` is registered in the `frag_only_func_defs`, which are checked in a few places in the shader_language file in combination with the `is_supported_frag_only_funcs` variable:
> 
> https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e531f3eb7b13a9adaaf5b15ac9b3aebc4c2030cd/servers/rendering/shader_language.cpp#L9129C2-L9130C89
> 
> https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e531f3eb7b13a9adaaf5b15ac9b3aebc4c2030cd/servers/rendering/shader_language.cpp#L6248C7-L6264C8
> 
> `shader_identifier_type` is deliberately not checked/set to anything when processing gdshaderinc files.
> 
> Options include:
> 
>     * Perform a similar `shader_type_identifier != StringName()` check specifically for this built-in validation.
> 
>     * Include `is_shader_inc` or empty shader_type_identifier in the criteria for `is_supported_frag_only_funcs` (broader impact).
> 
>     * Ignore it because it doesn't actually break shader compilation (though it is very confusing for a user, and similar to the linked issue will obfuscate "actual" errors lower down in the include).

this is also true for `discard` and probably other functions as well in addition to what's mentioned here and in the other issue.

in short, it's a bigger issue with gdshaderinc files and makes them very unwieldy and potentially impossible to debug (with no way to explicitly ignore the error, it stops error checking for the rest of the file)

I've submitted a PR that fixes this exactly the same way #89479 did. That PR only fixed 3 specific errors but my PR should fix the rest, as those are all due to is_supported_frag_only_funcs or is_discard_supported.
